text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE - p99 spike detected on continuous-batching serving path. Alerting teams, paging oncall.

jordan_sre: I'm on it. seeing p95 ~ 220ms, p99 up to 2.1s on cont-batch nodes in us-west-2. Streaming stalls reported by a few customers.

marta_infra: triage: tails coincide with mixed sequence length workloads. Batch sizes hitting max, then long KV cache lookups amplify latency. Metrics: batch_size distribution skewed — heavy 1-token + long-ctx combos.

alex_runtime: Logs show a cluster of requests with seq len 8 followed by 512 causing padding amplification. Scheduler isn't preempting small urgent streaming requests. This matches continuous-batching hot path.

emily_prodeng: Customer impact? any 5xx or UI timeouts reported to support?

rahul_support: We have 3 customers with UI timeouts and one reported aborted streaming sessions. No data exfiltration. Severity P1 due to visible customer UX regressions.

jordan_sre: Trying quick mitigations: lowering max_batch_size on streaming pool from 32 -> 8 to reduce coalescing delays. Applying to canary node now.

oncall-bot: opsbot: deploying config change to cont-batch-streaming pool (max_batch_size=8) to canary-target-3.

marta_infra: Canary shows immediate p99 improvement: 2.1s -> 650ms on canary node. However overall cluster effect limited because only 3 of 24 nodes updated.

alex_runtime: Another lever: enable scheduler fairshare preemption flag to favor streaming short requests. Config: `sched.enable_fair_preempt=true` and `sched.preempt_target=0.2` — can try on next canary.

jordan_sre: Rolling preempt flag to next 4 nodes. Monitoring KV eviction churn — want to avoid thrashing.

rahul_support: Notifying affected customers with temporary workaround recommendation: reduce concurrent streaming window or switch to non-streaming API for urgent paths.

emily_prodeng: Good to have short message for customer comms. Keep it factual: investigating latency spikes, temporary routing to fallback models, working on permanent fix.

oncall-bot: alert: cluster-wide p99 still above SLO on legacy streaming pool. Triggering paging to runtime and infra.

alex_runtime: Inspecting batcher logs: found pack-shed events where a large request blocked subsequent small streaming requests for ~700-900ms. Scheduler LIFO behavior composes badly with mixed lengths.

marta_infra: Propose immediate mitigation bundle: 1) max_batch_size->8 on streaming pools 2) enable fair_preempt on streaming scheduler 3) lower batch_coalesce_ms from 15 -> 6 for streaming route 4) route heavy seq workloads to dedicated batch pools.

jordan_sre: Implemented 1 & 3 across streaming pools. 2 is rolling. Routing change will need routing rules update + canary.

oncall-bot: opsbot: change applied: batch_coalesce_ms=6 on streaming pools. Confirmed rollout to 80% of streaming capacity.

rahul_support: Seeing immediate drop in aborted streaming sessions reports. Customers who had timeouts are now reporting improved behavior.

alex_runtime: Note: lowering coalesce_ms may increase token cost for small requests. Track cost delta. But priority is SLO restoration.

marta_infra: Observed a secondary issue: KV cache thrash when we reduce batch sizes for long-context requests. Need to tune KV eviction policy (increase rank-preserve window) or offload large-ctx to separate lane.

jordan_sre: For now, add rule to route requests with seq_len > 256 to heavy-ctx pool which uses dedicated batching profile (max_batch_size=16, no coalesce for streaming). Pushing routing update now.

oncall-bot: opsbot: routing rule applied to edge: seq_len>256 -> heavy-ctx-pool (canary first).

emily_prodeng: Customer impact update: 3 customers initially affected; two confirmed improved, one still seeing intermittent 95th spikes in Europe region. Investigating regional capacity/fallback.

alex_runtime: Europe nodes show similar pattern but delayed by ~2x. Might be due to different traffic mix and larger average seq lengths for that tenant.

marta_infra: Next steps: 1) full rollout of fair_preempt if canary stable 2) permanent scheduler change to prioritize short streaming lanes (design doc follow-up) 3) KV cache policy adjustments and telemetry to detect mixed-len pack events 4) post-incident RCA and customer outreach.

jordan_sre: Handoff to night oncall: marta and alex will take persistent tasks. Leaving checkpointed runbook in #oncall-playbooks.

marta_infra: Handoff notes: current state — streaming p99 improved from 2.1s -> ~600-800ms cluster-wide after bundle. Cost increase ~+6% token compute for streaming. Routing heavy-ctx pool in place. Fair_preempt can be toggled if regression seen.

alex_runtime: Action items assigned: runtime to implement pack-aware scheduling (medium-term), infra to tune KV eviction, prodeng to draft customer comms and update affected customers tomorrow.

rahul_support: I'll follow up with the still-impacted EU customer with a targeted workaround and ETA.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated, page_state=handed_off, mitigations=applied. Please file postmortem and link here.

emily_prodeng: Thanks team. Please add timeline + graphs (p95/p99, batch_size dist, coalesce_ms change) to the postmortem. We'll prepare customer-facing timeline.

jordan_sre: Closing handoff. Marking incident for RCA and follow-ups. Leaving logs and config diffs in /var/ops/incident-3765432199.

marta_infra: I'll own the follow-up scheduler change PR. ETA EOD tomorrow.

alex_runtime: I'll add pack-detection telemetry and draft a mitigation that avoids padding amplification (approx plan in doc linked: https://internal.redwood/notes/pack-aware-sched).

rahul_support: Notifying the remaining customer now.

oncall-bot: incident closed to active mitigation channel. Remember to tag postmortem with severity and customer impact metrics.
